evidence: src/business/services/MileageService.ts: `constructor(private readonly prisma: PrismaService)` is injected, yet `averageDaily` runs `const prisma = new PrismaClient();` and queries `prisma.mileage.findMany`, which bypasses the injected PrismaService.

src/business/services/MileageService.ts: `record(plate, km, lastServiceKm)` returns `km - lastServiceKm >= SERVICE_INTERVAL_KM`. It recomputes the service-due rule from a constant imported from ../model/Vehicle, using a lastServiceKm the caller supplies instead of the Vehicle aggregate.

src/business/services/MaintenanceService.ts: it works through the injected `VehicleTable`/`WorkOrderTable` gateways and through domain methods (`vehicle.takeOutOfService()`, `vehicle.returnToService()`, `order.log`, `order.finish`, `order.overrun()`), and it loads aggregates through its private `vehicle()`/`order()` helpers.
The two files take different routes to persistence: MaintenanceService uses table gateways, while MileageService uses raw Prisma calls (`this.prisma.mileage.create`, `new PrismaClient()`).
parsedVerdict.reasoning: Both services cover the fleet-maintenance concern, but they don't share the same abstractions. MaintenanceService works through injected table gateways (VehicleTable, WorkOrderTable), rebuilds Vehicle and WorkOrder domain objects, and leaves state changes to the domain (takeOutOfService, returnToService, log, finish, overrun). MileageService does neither. Its averageDaily method creates its own `new PrismaClient()` and so skips the PrismaService it already receives in its constructor. That bypasses the module's own injection abstraction, and the class ends up using two different ways to reach the data. MileageService also reads Prisma directly instead of going through a table gateway like the rest of the module. Finally, record() works out whether a vehicle is due for service with its own arithmetic on SERVICE_INTERVAL_KM, using a lastServiceKm value the caller passes in. The Vehicle model owns lastServiceKm and the interval constant, so the service-due rule probably belongs on Vehicle. Computing it in the service spreads that rule outside the domain object, and the service never loads the Vehicle aggregate the way MaintenanceService does. I can't see Vehicle.ts, so whether a matching method already exists there is an inference.

violations.message: averageDaily creates `new PrismaClient()` instead of using the injected `this.prisma` (PrismaService). This bypasses the module's own dependency abstraction, and the class ends up with two different ways to reach the data.

record() works out whether service is due with `km - lastServiceKm >= SERVICE_INTERVAL_KM`, using a lastServiceKm the caller passes in. The rule should stay with the Vehicle model, which owns lastServiceKm and SERVICE_INTERVAL_KM, not be computed again in the service. This also differs from MaintenanceService, which loads Vehicle and calls its methods.
